text:
Marcus Lin: Dropping this here: security packet draft for AWS/GCP marketplace is in review. Before PMM submits anything, we need to align on (1) approvals (who signs off), and (2) what evidence we can share w/ partner reviewers vs customers, esp. SOC2 + pen test. Link is in the drive folder but please comment inline and summarize here.

Soojin Lee: thx @Marcus. I’m trying to get final language locked by EOW for listing attachments. Biggest questions from Partnerships: “SOC2/ISO?” “KMS?” “audit logs?” and a simple data retention statement. Also AWS asked if we can attach a “security overview PDF” directly to listing.

Olga Petrov: Quick flag: we should NOT attach SOC 2 Type II report directly to the listing. That’s NDA-only. We can attach a one-pager that says “SOC 2 Type II available under NDA upon request” + provide a request email/portal.

Dr. Aisha Rahman: +1. Also no screenshots of the auditor letterhead in public attachments. AWS/GCP reviewers may ask; we can provide in partner portal under their confidentiality terms, but treat it as “restricted” not “public.”

Naomi Feldman: Can someone confirm the current status language for ISO? Packet currently says “ISO 27001 compliant.” That’s not accurate.

Marcus Lin: Correct, ISO is not certified. We should change to “ISO 27001-aligned controls” / “ISO 27001 program in progress” (whatever we can substantiate) OR remove entirely.

Olga Petrov: Remove entirely from marketplace docs unless Legal is ok with “in progress” wording. “Aligned” is squishy unless we have a mapping doc ready to share.

Soojin Lee: Got it. I’ll strike ISO claims from the packet + listing copy.

Ethan Park: From an eng perspective, packet says “Customer-managed KMS keys supported.” That’s only true for Private (VPC/on-prem) deployments w/ customer-managed infra. Hosted API uses AWS-managed KMS on our side; Dedicated depends on the environment. We need to be precise.

Marcus Lin: Thank you. Proposed language:
- Hosted/Dedicated: “Encryption at rest using cloud provider KMS-managed keys (service-managed).”
- Private: “Customer-managed keys supported (KMS/HSM integrations available) depending on deployment model.”
Avoid “BYOK everywhere.”

Rafael Mendes: Also audit logs: we have control plane audit logs (org changes, API key creation/rotation, model deployments, entitlement changes) + request logs for inference (metadata). We do NOT log full prompt/response by default, but some customers turn on extended logs in Private. Packet currently implies “full request/response always logged” which is risky.

Marcus Lin: Yeah, that needs correction. We should say:
- “Audit logs for administrative/control plane actions available in Console”
- “Request logging configurable; content logging is opt-in and environment-dependent.”

Elliot Price: Doc-wise, we’ll need consistent phrasing between the packet + the marketplace security FAQ + docs site pages. If we decide on the above, I can propagate it.

Chloe Martin: On retention: what are we comfortable stating? Packet says “logs retained 1 year.” That’s not true for all tiers.

Rafael Mendes: Default Hosted retention for platform logs is 30 days in prod today. Some enterprise add-ons extend retention. For Private, customer controls retention.

Naomi Feldman: So we should say:
- “Default retention: 30 days for Hosted platform logs (may vary by plan); longer retention available as an add-on; Private deployments are customer-configured.”
And avoid hard numbers in public docs unless we’re ready to commit contractually.

Dr. Aisha Rahman: Agree. In marketplace context, if we mention an exact retention period, Procurement will treat it as a commitment.

Soojin Lee: Understood. I’ll remove the “1 year” statement and change to “default retention varies by plan; longer retention available.”

Marcus Lin: Evidence sharing: my recommendation:
Public / attachable to marketplace listing:
- Security overview PDF (controls summary, shared responsibility, high-level diagrams without sensitive internals)
- A “Compliance posture” page (SOC2 Type II statement + NDA note)
- Pen test “attestation letter” ONLY (no full report)
- Data processing/security contacts
Restricted / NDA-only:
- Full SOC2 report
- Full pen test report
- Detailed network diagrams / threat model
- Vendor pentest scope details

Olga Petrov: +1. Also: for AWS/GCP reviewers specifically, we can provide restricted docs via partner portal if required for review, but still treat as “confidential” and track who we sent it to.

SecurityBot: Reminder: use the Security Evidence Request workflow for sharing restricted artifacts externally. Owners: @Olga Petrov (GRC), @Marcus Lin (SecEng). Link: https://redwoodinference.example/security/evidence-request

Soojin Lee: For the AWS attachment, can we include the encryption diagram currently in the packet? It shows “multi-region control plane” and some service names.

Marcus Lin: Let’s redact service names + internal component labels. Keep it at “API gateway -> control plane -> inference clusters” level. No account IDs, no VPC IDs, no internal DNS.

Ethan Park: I can provide a sanitized version of the diagram today. The current one includes internal queue names.

Naomi Feldman: Approval workflow: can we confirm who needs to sign off? I assume Aisha + Marcus + Olga, and PMM acknowledges final wording.

Dr. Aisha Rahman: For this packet: SecEng (Marcus) verifies technical accuracy, GRC (Olga) verifies compliance language/evidence handling, and I give final sign-off. PMM can submit after that.

Olga Petrov: Also please add a footer disclaimer: “Information is subject to change; specific controls may vary by deployment model (Hosted, Dedicated, Private).” That helps reduce misinterpretation.

Elliot Price: I’ll add that disclaimer consistently across the docs + packet.

Soojin Lee: Timeline: can I get sign-off by Thursday 3pm PT? Partnerships wants to submit to AWS Friday.

Marcus Lin: If we lock edits today, yes. Action items:
1) @Soojin Lee remove ISO claim + retention hard number; adjust SOC2 to “available under NDA.”
2) @Ethan Park deliver sanitized encryption diagram.
3) @Rafael Mendes sanity check audit logging + retention phrasing.
4) @Olga Petrov confirm latest SOC2 period language + evidence request instructions.
Then I’ll do final pass and send to @Dr. Aisha Rahman for approval.

Rafael Mendes: I’ll review tonight. Also we should avoid saying “SLA-backed uptime/latency” in the security packet; that belongs in commercial terms.

Soojin Lee: ack, will keep it security-only.

Olga Petrov: One more nit: “HIPAA” is mentioned in a FAQ block as “HIPAA ready.” Please remove. We can say “We support regulated workloads; contact us for compliance requirements.”

Marcus Lin: Good catch. Removing.

Dr. Aisha Rahman: Thanks all. Once updated, tag me in the doc. I’ll sign off as long as: no ISO claims, no public SOC2 attachments, KMS language is scoped by deployment mode, and audit logging is accurate.

Soojin Lee: :thumbsup: will update and ping.

Ethan Park: Sanitized diagram ETA ~2 hrs. I’ll drop a link here.

Marcus Lin: Perfect. Please also note in the packet that for Private deployments, customer is responsible for network boundary + key management if self-hosted. Shared responsibility section should be explicit.

Naomi Feldman: I’ll add a short “Shared responsibility” table (Hosted vs Dedicated vs Private) but keep it high-level.

Dr. Aisha Rahman: Great. Keep it concise.

Marcus Lin: Closing loop: once we approve, let’s also store the final PDF in the “marketplace-security-packet” folder with version/date. We need a paper trail for future reviews.

Olga Petrov: +1 and add refresh cadence note (quarterly) + owner.

Elliot Price: I’ll handle versioning + link updates in docs.

Soojin Lee: ok, edits in progress now. Will re-share by EOD.
